findings.title: Fallback locales are never loaded outside of the ApplicationController#set_locale path
findings.body: I18n.translate loads only `config.locale` (line 68) before delegating to the real translate, which will now walk the fallback chain defined by FallbackLocaleList (user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en). The fallback locales are only pre-loaded via ApplicationController#set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call. Any translation performed outside a web request — background jobs (Sidekiq), mailers, rake tasks, one-off scripts — will look up keys in fallback locales that were never loaded, so the Fallbacks backend will return 'translation missing' strings instead of the English/default text. The accelerator should ensure all fallback locales for the current locale are loaded inside `translate`/`load_locale`, not rely on the controller filter.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, serving stale translations after default_locale changes
findings.body: The cache key is built from `key`, `config.locale` and the backend object id. With this PR the effective translation for a given I18n.locale also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (via FallbackLocaleList#[]). When an admin changes default_locale at runtime, the fallback order changes but the cache key does not, so previously cached results from the old fallback chain keep being served for up to LRU_CACHE_SIZE (300) entries until they age out. There is no I18n.reload!/cache invalidation hooked to the default_locale SiteSetting in this change, so users in a non-default locale will continue seeing translations from the old default locale. The key should incorporate the fallback locales (or the cache should be cleared when default_locale changes).

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but only overrides [], so all other Hash behaviors report it as empty
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList is a Hash whose lookup semantics are entirely in `[]`, with no stored entries. Any code in the i18n gem, Rails, or plugins that interacts with `I18n.fallbacks` through Hash methods other than `[]` (e.g. `each`, `key?`, `keys`, `merge!`, `store`) will see an empty hash: per-locale fallback rules configured that way are silently dropped, and any code that iterates the fallbacks map (for preloading, validation, or locale resolution) will do nothing. Subclassing Hash while making `[]` lie about the contents is fragile; a plain object responding to `[]` (and to whatever the i18n version in use requires) would be safer, or the entries should actually be stored in the hash.

findings.title: Fallback lookup dereferences SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation, which is not safe during boot or before SiteSetting is available
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every translation lookup. During application boot (initializers, eager loading, asset precompilation) or in contexts where the settings table/connection is not available, SiteSetting may raise or return nil; `nil.to_sym` yields a symbol that then goes through the load path and could trigger DB queries or errors at times when translations are used before the app is fully initialized. A safer approach is to memoize the fallback list and only refresh it when the setting actually changes, and to guard against SiteSetting being unavailable.

findings.title: Initializer relies on implicit filename ordering ('order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb') which is fragile
findings.body: The comment at the top states the file must load after 02-freedom_patches.rb, and this happens to work because Rails loads initializers alphabetically and digits sort before letters. But the i18n initializer's `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` must apply to the backend class before it is used, and the pluralization include replaces the removed config/initializers/pluralization.rb — whose old filename sorted before i18n.rb, so any load-order dependent behavior (e.g. plugins or freedom patches touching I18n) silently depends on string sort order. If anyone renames this file (e.g. to `20-i18n.rb` or adds a locale-related initializer), the ordering requirement breaks with no error. The dependency should be explicit (require the freedom patch file, or use config.initializer with `before`/`after`), not a comment.
